The guests all seem to appreciate her menu apart from Amir.

programme.title: Come Dine with Me

programme.title: Come Dine with Me

programme.title: Villages by the Sea
programme.desc: Ben Robinson travels to Cushendall, one of the finest planned Georgian villages in Northern Ireland. It was owned and shaped by a series of owners but most notably its 19th-century merchant landlord Francis Turnly. The forward-thinking man hoped to try out his ideas for a new global order - ideas akin to such organisations as today's UN and the WHO. programme.title: Canal Boat Diaries

programme.title: Remembers...

programme.title: Rome: A History of the Eternal City
programme.desc: Historian Simon Sebag Montefiore uncovers the central role played by religion in creating and maintaining the power of the city of Rome from its foundations to the modern day. In the first episode we see how every event in ancient Rome revolved around religion. From the foundation myth through to the deification of Emperors; nothing could happen without calling upon the Pantheon of Roman gods.

programme.title: Mary Beard's Ultimate Rome: Empire Without Limit
programme.desc: Mary takes an in-depth look at the question of identity and citizenship within the Roman Empire. What did it mean to be, or to become, Roman, and how did the very different parts of the Empire react to Roman rule? In the beautifully-preserved cities of Algeria, incomers and locals mixed to create flourishing communities with a distinct `more Roman than Rome' frontier identity.

programme.title: I, Claudius

programme.desc: In the final programme of the series, Jamie Oliver cooks his versions of three comfort food classics. There's ham, egg and chips, with a Jamaican jerk rub for the ham and served with caramelized pineapple. His ultimate chicken kebab is served with hummus and mango amba sauce.

programme.title: The Pioneer Woman
programme.desc: It's question time on the ranch and Ree is covering topics ranging from recipes and romance, to fashion and ranch favourites. Her answers include three meat, three bean, three chilli chilli, shrimp mango lettuce cups, and linguine with clam sauce.

programme.title: The Pioneer Woman
programme.desc: Cinnamon rolls, prime rib with rosemary, Duchess potatoes, Burgundy mushrooms and whiskey cream sauce.

programme.title: James Martin's Islands to Highlands
programme.desc: James takes a magical trip to the stunning Isle of Skye, where he's joined by top chef and ultimate Scotsman Tony Singh. Tony visits a local bakery which doubles as an art gallery and learns to make the local oatcakes. James is inspired by the amazing local seafood and cooks up a tasty dish using plaice and lovage. Their day comes to a perfect end aboard a boat, where they spot dozens of dolphins, and James cooks up a fresh lobster and langoustine dish with an added Scottish twist.

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: It's Bread Week, with the 10 bakers having much to prove with a fruity teatime Signature, a rather international-flavoured Technical, and an ambitious Showstopper.

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: It's Dessert Week and the bakers must create a cracking meringue Signature, a wobbly Technical, and a complex chocolate Showstopper that promises to reveal all.

programme.title: Michel Roux's French Country Cooking
programme.desc: Michel makes mouth-watering pork steaks with asparagus and courgettes. Later, he demonstrates how to cook the perfect souffléed cheese omelette.

programme.title: Jamie's One-Pan Wonders
programme.desc: Jamie Oliver shows us how to make easy and delicious meals cooked in just one pan, pot or dish, starting with frying-pan pasta, a twist on a fish pie and a sublime roast lamb feast.

programme.title: Jamie's One-Pan Wonders
programme.desc: Jamie Oliver shows us how to make a super-fast, flavoursome smoky noodle soup, the cleverest home-made bread and a chicken and mushroom pie with a time-saving tip for perfect pastry.

programme.desc: Climbing into a realm of thin air and towering rock as mythical monkeys battle for a winter food stash, lemurs fill a fruit-filled tree canopy, and aromatic trees bring together blossom and possum in a moonlit tryst.

programme.title: Nomads of the Serengeti
programme.desc: Jean Du Plessis takes you on an exhilarating trip through the Serengeti with migrating wildebeest.

programme.title: Rooted
programme.desc: The Namaqua Rock Fig Tree stands rooted on the slope of a rocky hill in Namaqualand, South Africa. It is the ultimate survivor, able to withstand the unforgiving conditions in a landscape facing ever rising temperatures and less and less rainfall each year.

programme.title: Great Parks of Africa
programme.desc: Augrabies is where the mighty Orange River plunges over the awesome 56 meter Augrabies waterfall. Derived from a word oukurubes which means place of thunder in the indigenous language of the Nama-Khoi this land is the heart of a harsh and sun-beaten world with flashes of brilliant color and a thunderous roar.

programme.title: Slovenia: Where Nature Comes First
programme.desc: The filmmaker sheds light on the captivating nature, wildlife and landscapes in Slovenia, where humans have learnt how to coexist with nature without affecting its beauty.

programme.desc: Michael Portillo ventures down under to experience one of the world's greatest rail journeys aboard the legendary Ghan Railway. programme.title: Great Australian Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo explores New South Wales, steered by his 1913 Bradshaw's Guide. He strikes west into the Blue Mountains and travels 570 miles into the interior of the vast Australian continent to reach the mining city of Broken Hill. In the waterside metropolis of Sydney, the NSW capital, Michael investigates the origins of the city as a penal colony, visiting the Hyde Park Barracks, where many of the first convicts were housed.
